May: The Perfect Riding Month

Many experienced UK motorcycle tourers consider May the finest riding month. The days are long (5am to 9pm), temperatures are warm but not hot, the landscape is at its greenest, and crucially — school holidays haven't started. The roads are quiet, the weather is often excellent, and the countryside is at peak beauty.

Conditions

  • Temperature: Average 10-17°C. Warm spells can reach 22°C+. Mountain areas remain cool.
  • Daylight: 5am-9pm. Over 16 hours of useful light — enough for epic day rides.
  • Roads: Dry, clean, warm tarmac. The best riding surface of the year.

Why May Is Special

  • Bluebells: The UK's bluebell woods are at their peak in May. Forest rides through carpets of blue are magical.
  • Bank holidays: Early May and late May bank holidays give long weekends for touring.
  • Pre-tourist season: The Highlands, Lakes, and Snowdonia are accessible and empty compared to July and August.
  • Wildlife: Nesting birds, young animals, and the countryside teeming with life.

May Touring Destinations

  • Scottish Highlands: May is often the best month for Highland riding — long days, relatively dry, no midges yet (they arrive in late May/June). The NC500 and Highland passes are at their finest.
  • Snowdonia: Warm enough for comfortable mountain pass riding, quiet enough for enjoyable roads.
  • Lake District: The fells are green, the lakes are still, and the passes are clear. Pre-half-term May is the Lakes at their best.

May Bank Holiday Rides

Both May bank holidays are ideal for two or three-day tours:

  • Early May bank holiday: Ride south — Devon, Cornwall, Dorset in spring sunshine.
  • Late May bank holiday: Ride north — Yorkshire Dales, Lake District, Scottish Borders.
If you can only take one week off for motorcycle touring in the UK, make it late May. The combination of weather, daylight, quiet roads, and landscape beauty is unmatched at any other time of year.

May Bank Holiday Tours

Both May bank holidays provide ideal long-weekend touring opportunities. The early May bank holiday falls when spring is fully established across southern and central England — perfect for a Peak District, Cotswolds, or Dorset coast tour.

The late May bank holiday coincides with the start of the Scottish touring season. A three-day dash to the Highlands and back is ambitious but achievable, or a more relaxed tour of the Scottish Borders and Northumberland makes excellent use of the long weekend. Book accommodation early — biker-friendly B&Bs fill up for bank holiday weekends.

Easter Weather Contingency

Always have a wet-weather plan for Easter. British Easter weather is notoriously unreliable, ranging from snow to heatwave. Build indoor activities into each day's plan — a castle visit, museum stop, or long pub lunch — so a rainy morning doesn't ruin the day.

Easter is also the traditional start of the campsite season, with many UK campsites opening for the Easter weekend. If you're a camping tourer, Easter is your first opportunity to test gear after winter storage. Shake out the tent, check for damage, and make sure your stove and sleeping bag are in good condition.

Church services on Easter Sunday create a unique atmosphere in small rural villages across Britain. Even if you're not religious, the community gathering and the flower-decorated churches add a special dimension to a touring stop in a traditional village.

Essential Easter Packing

Easter weather is wildly unpredictable. Pack as if you're touring in winter and hope for spring. Heated grips, thermal base layers, waterproof over-suit, and winter gloves should all be in your luggage even if the forecast looks mild. A sunny Easter morning can turn to sleet by afternoon, and being caught cold and wet 100 miles from home is miserable.

Carry cash alongside your cards — many rural B&Bs, campsites, and village shops over Easter weekend may have limited card payment facilities, especially if temporary signal boosters for busy periods haven't been set up. A small amount of cash covers parking, honesty-box campsites, and church donation boxes.

Easter also marks the opening of many seasonal tourist attractions — castles, gardens, and stately homes that close over winter reopen for the Easter weekend. Check opening dates and plan your route around any sites you want to visit, as Easter is often the first chance to see them after the winter closure. keyTakeaways: May is widely rated the finest riding month: 10-17C, warm spells to 22C-plus, and over 16 hours of daylight.
School holidays have not started, so the Highlands, Lakes and Snowdonia are accessible and empty.
Bluebell woods peak in May, making forest rides magical.
The Scottish Highlands are at their best with long days, relatively dry weather and no midges yet.
Two bank holidays give ideal long weekends: ride south early May, north late May.

comparisonTable.caption: Why May is the perfect riding month

faq.q: Why is May considered the best month to ride in the UK?
faq.a: Many experienced tourers rate May the finest riding month because the combination is unmatched: days run from 5am to 9pm, temperatures are warm but not hot, the landscape is at its greenest and school holidays have not started. The roads are quiet, the weather is often excellent and the tarmac is dry, clean and warm. If you can only take one week off, make it late May.

faq.q: Is May a good time to ride the Scottish Highlands?
faq.a: May is often the best month for Highland riding. The days are long, the weather is relatively dry, the light is clear and, crucially, the midges have not yet arrived because they emerge in late May and June. The NC500 and the Highland passes are at their finest, and the roads are empty compared with July and August.

faq.q: How should I use the May bank holidays?
faq.a: Both May bank holidays are ideal for two or three-day tours. On the early May bank holiday ride south to Devon, Cornwall or Dorset in spring sunshine, or the Peak District and Cotswolds. The late May bank holiday coincides with the start of the Scottish season, so consider a dash to the Highlands or a relaxed tour of the Borders and Northumberland. Book biker-friendly B&Bs early.

faq.q: What makes May special beyond the weather?
faq.a: May delivers peak natural beauty. The UK's bluebell woods are at their peak, so forest rides pass through carpets of blue. The countryside teems with nesting birds and young animals, and pre-tourist-season access means the Highlands, Lakes and Snowdonia feel private. Snowdonia is warm enough for comfortable mountain-pass riding while remaining quiet.

faq.q: Do I still need to prepare for cold in May?
faq.a: Mountain areas remain cool even in a warm May, so carry a layer for altitude. The far south can hit 22C-plus while a Highland pass stays chilly, so a flexible layering system is sensible. Otherwise May offers the best riding surface of the year, and the main planning task is booking accommodation before bank-holiday demand fills the best places.
